skill.name: push-notifications
skill.description: Set up, toggle, and test ntfy push notifications. Receive mobile alerts when coding agents finish on macOS, Linux, or Windows.
skill.summary: Send ntfy alerts when terminal or VS Code coding agents finish work.
skill.author: lc700x

security_audit.summary: Most of the 285 signals are documentation markers, fixed commands, expected configuration paths, or standard output redirection. Confirmed risks include privileged installation, persistent hooks, shared temporary files, broad process termination, and unencrypted notification delivery. No prompt injection was found, but transport and process controls need correction before broad publication.

remediation.issue: Plaintext notification transport exposes the ntfy topic and repository metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Use an explicit HTTPS URL, reject TLS failures, and support a trusted self-hosted endpoint.

remediation.issue: Hooks, command wrappers, and login profiles create persistent execution paths.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval, show exact diffs, preserve backups, and provide precise removal steps.

remediation.issue: The setup includes privileged package installation commands.
remediation.suggestion: Request confirmation before sudo and present manual installation as an optional prerequisite.

remediation.issue: Predictable shared temporary files allow tampering, deletion, or arithmetic injection.
remediation.suggestion: Use a private runtime directory with restrictive permissions and remove only files created by the watcher.

remediation.issue: Daemon shutdown trusts stale PID files and uses broad pkill patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Validate process identity before signaling and track only child processes created by this daemon.

remediation.issue: Shell wrappers replace the coding agent exit status with the notification result.
remediation.suggestion: Save the agent status, send the notification, and return the original status.

semantic_findings.title: Unencrypted Notification Transport Exposes Topic and Metadata
semantic_findings.description: The curl target omits an HTTPS scheme, so curl defaults to plaintext HTTP. It sends the bearer-like topic, project directory, and optional git statistics.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The executed curl URL is ntfy.sh/${TOPIC} without https://, while the request body contains workspace metadata. The README confirms the topic is the only authentication.

semantic_findings.title: Shell Wrappers Discard Agent Exit Status
semantic_findings.description: The wrapper runs notify.sh after the agent command, so the notification result replaces the agent exit status. Automation can treat failed work as successful.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The wrapper calls command copilot and then notify.sh without saving and restoring the first command status. notify.sh exits with status zero.

content.user_title: Get Push Alerts When Coding Agents Finish
content.value_statement: Long coding tasks can finish while you are away from the computer. This skill sends ntfy mobile alerts and optional local sounds.
actual_capabilities: Creates a random ntfy topic and displays a QR subscription code.
Configures Claude Code Stop hooks and command wrappers for terminal agents.
Watches Claude Code, Copilot Chat, and Codex VS Code extension logs.
Sends mobile notifications and plays platform-specific local sounds.
Supports setup, testing, status checks, agent management, and one-command toggling.
limitations: Mobile delivery requires the ntfy app and an external or self-hosted ntfy service.
The Windows VS Code watcher requires Git Bash or WSL.
Copilot and Codex log markers indicate activity, not reliable turn completion.
Detailed alerts may include project names and git statistics, so sensitive repositories need extra review.

use_cases.title: Monitor Long Agent Tasks
use_cases.description: Receive a phone alert when a terminal coding agent completes a long task.

use_cases.title: Track VS Code Assistants
use_cases.description: Run one watcher for Claude Code, Copilot Chat, and Codex extension activity.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Alerts
use_cases.description: Configure a self-hosted ntfy endpoint and consistent completion alerts across supported platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Notifications
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up push notifications for my installed coding agents. Detect my platform, explain each change, and ask before editing configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Add One Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Add notifications for [agent]. Preserve existing hooks and shell functions, then send a test alert.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Missing Alerts
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my notification topic, script permissions, configured hooks, and watcher status. Report the cause before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Harden Self-Hosted Delivery
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure my ntfy server at [HTTPS URL]. Minimize notification details, secure local files, and review every persistent process.

output_examples.input: Set up alerts for Claude Code on macOS.
output: A protected ntfy topic was created.
The Claude Code Stop hook is ready for approval.
The VS Code watcher is not running.

output_examples.input: Why are Codex VS Code alerts frequent?
output_examples.output: Codex uses an activity marker, so multiple log events can trigger alerts. Increase debounce time or disable the watcher.

best_practices: Use a random topic, restrict its file permissions, and rotate it after accidental disclosure.
Review and approve every hook, shell profile edit, and daemon before activation.
Use HTTPS or a trusted self-hosted ntfy server before sending repository details.
anti_patterns: Do not commit, publish, or display the full ntfy topic in shared logs.
Do not enable detailed alerts for sensitive repositories without reviewing transmitted metadata.
Do not auto-start watchers or run privileged installation commands without explicit approval.

faq.question: Which coding agents are supported?
faq.answer: The skill covers Claude Code, Codex, Copilot, aider, and other terminal agents through hooks, wrappers, or log watching.

faq.question: Does it work on Windows?
faq.answer: Yes. Terminal integrations work on Windows, while the VS Code watcher requires Git Bash or WSL.

faq.question: Is an ntfy account required?
faq.answer: No account is required for public ntfy topics. Treat the random topic as a secret.

faq.question: Can I use a private ntfy server?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace the default service endpoint with your trusted HTTPS server.

faq.question: What information is sent?
faq.answer: Alerts include the agent label and project directory. Detailed mode also includes file counts and git statistics.

faq.question: How are all alerts disabled?
faq.answer: The off command removes execute permission from the notification script, disabling every configured integration.
